title: Investigate and remediate output coalescer collapse during capacity surges
creator: Aisha Walker
description:
Summary:
During a weekend capacity surge (2026-02-27 03:40 UTC) we observed a class of streaming failures that manifested as abrupt client disconnects and partial token deliveries for ~17 minutes across three regions. Affected customers saw incomplete streaming responses and session resets which caused visible product regressions in chat features and increased client-side retry volume.

What happened (brief):
- A recent change to the output coalescer (coalescer dedup optimization, rolled 2026-02-20) reduced per-fragment deduping CPU but introduced a pathological path when inbound fanout exceeded a concurrent-window threshold.
- Under sustained surge, coalescer worker goroutines were starved by blocking I/O and internal queues filled; backpressure signals amplified across fanout layers leading to opaque disconnects and partial token emission to clients.
- KV-cache lookups for resumed sessions sometimes returned stale prefix fragments which caused the runtime to mark fragments as "in-flight" but never fully commit them; this increased queue pressure.

Impact:
- Regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-2 (partial).
- Duration: 2026-02-27 03:40 UTC -> 2026-02-27 03:57 UTC (mitigated)
- Customers affected: ~42 customers with >5K active streaming sessions; top 5 customers reported UI errors and elevated error budgets.

Immediate mitigations applied (on-call):
1) Reverted coalescer dedup optimization (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4172).
2) Throttled per-session concurrent stream fanout at the routing layer to 6 concurrent fanouts.
3) Increased internal coalescer queue capacity by 2x and enabled more aggressive eviction for stale fragments.
These mitigations restored stability within 17 minutes but are not acceptable long-term fixes (performance and cost regressions observed).

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- Primary: Output coalescer optimization introduced a lock ordering and queueing pattern that behaved poorly when request fanout distribution had a long-tail (multiple downstream subscribers per session).
- Secondary: Backpressure propagation lacked smoothing and allowed oscillation: short bursts triggered global throttles which in turn caused more bursts when throttles released.
- Tertiary: KV cache TTL/consistency gap allowed resumed sessions to re-introduce stale fragments into the coalescer pipeline, compounding queue pressure.

Proposed long-term action items (owner + ETA):
A1) Implement bounded coalescer worker pool with adaptive spill-to-disk for overflow (owner: Marco Chen, ETA: 2026-04-01).
A2) Add backpressure smoothing: exponentially-weighted moving average for upstream signals and a token-bucket-based rate limiter at fanout ingress (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026-03-29).
A3) KV cache consistency hardening: ensure resume paths validate fragment commit IDs and proactively invalidate on mismatch (owner: Daniel Ortiz, ETA: 2026-03-22).
A4) Add e2e chaos tests that simulate heavy fanout + KV inconsistency for continuous integration (owner: QA Squad, ETA: 2026-03-26).
A5) Telemetry: Add coalescer queue depth, per-session fanout histogram, fragment-stale counts, and backpressure-signal-rate dashboards; create alert when queue depth > 80th percentile of baseline for 2m (owner: Observability team, ETA: 2026-03-10).
A6) Release gating: new coalescer optimizations require canary with synthetic fanout tests and traffic shaping; add rollout checklist (owner: Release Eng, ETA: 2026-03-18).

Acceptance criteria:
- No streaming disconnects in canary traffic with synthetic fanout up to 10x baseline for 30m.
- Coalescer queue depth stable under load tests; tail latency for streaming tokens <= baseline + 15%.
- No customer-facing partial-token regressions in the next SLA report; accepted by SRE and Product.

Notes and risks:
- Bound worker pool + spill-to-disk will reduce memory pressure but could increase tail latency; must be guarded by SLO-conditional configuration.
- Backpressure smoothing reduces oscillation but may increase end-to-end latency for bursty workloads; we will expose knob in Dedicated configs.

Deliverables:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Coalescer+Resilience+Design (draft attached to ticket).
- Hotfix PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4172 (revert)
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Walker: Created ticket from incident bridge notes. Initial triage indicates coalescer queue saturation under surge; prioritized P0.

2026-03-02 - Marco Chen: Reproduced queue-fill locally with synthetic fanout script (tools/chaos/fanout-stress). Observed worker goroutine count plateau and blocked syscall traces. Opening design spike for bounded pool.
2026-03-04 - Priya Nair: Prototype of backpressure smoothing implemented in feature/backpressure-ewma branch. Early results show 40% reduction in oscillation on replay tests.
2026-03-07 - Daniel Ortiz: KV resume path updated to check fragment commit IDs; added unit tests. Found two cases where stale fragments were accepted when commit_id==0.
2026-03-09 - On-call (Marcus Li): Deployed emergency throttles and reverted coalescer optimization. Incidents stopped but customer latency increased ~12%. Need long-term plan.
2026-03-11 - Observability team: Dashboards live in Grafana dashboard id 8721. Set alert coalescer_queue_depth: firing at 2026-03-11 10:34 UTC during canary run; helped validate thresholds.
2026-03-12 - Product (Leah Kim): Prioritize A2 and A3 for next patch release. Product requests clear rollout notes for Dedicated customers about new knobs.
2026-03-12 - Marco Chen: Created spike tasks: ENG-82135 (coalescer bounded pool spike), ENG-82136 (fanout ingress rate limiter). Adding as sub_issues.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Walker: Marking ticket In Progress; tracking owners and linking design doc. ETA for main deliverables: end of March.
